column1: divulge§He never divulged the source, and the four months he spent in prison for it are the reason people still trust the paper.§他始终没有**泄露**消息来源，为此坐的四个月牢正是人们至今信任这家报纸的原因。§di-（分开）+ vulg（大众，同 vulgar 通俗的）→ 抖给众人
docile§The most docile horse in the stable is also the one that has thrown two experienced riders this year.§马厩里最**温顺的**那匹马，也是今年掀下过两位老骑手的那匹。§doc（教，同 doctor 博士）→ 好教的
doctrinaire§His doctrinaire reading of the rules made the department unworkable and was never once formally overruled.§他对规则**教条式**的解读让这个部门无法运转，却一次也没被正式推翻。§doctrin（学说，同 doctrine 教义）
dogmatic§The most dogmatic person in the field changed his mind twice, and both times pretended he always had.§这个领域最**武断**的人改过两次主意，两次都装作自己一贯如此。§dogma（教条）
dogmatist§A dogmatist can be argued with; the trouble is that he treats every argument as an attack on his character.§跟**教条主义者**是能争论的，麻烦在于他把每次争论都当成对他人格的攻击。§
dominance§The company's dominance rests on one patent, and the patent expires in about four years.§这家公司的**支配地位**建立在一项专利上，而专利大约四年后到期。§domin（主人，同 dominate 支配）
dominant§The dominant species here arrived eighty years ago and now accounts for four fifths of the biomass.§这里的**优势**物种八十年前才到，如今占据五分之四的生物量。§
dominate§One voice dominated the discussion for ninety minutes, and the three quiet people had read the report.§一个声音**主导**了九十分钟的讨论，而那三个安静的人读过报告。§
dormant§The volcano lay dormant for six centuries, and the towns built on its slopes had forgotten it entirely.§这座火山**休眠**了六个世纪，建在其山坡上的城镇已经彻底忘了它。§dorm（睡，同 dormitory 宿舍）
doubtful§It is doubtful whether the treatment helps at all, and certain that it costs four thousand a course.§这种疗法是否有效**很可疑**，而每疗程四千块是确定的。§
dowager§The dowager controlled the estate for thirty years and left it, in the end, to the gardener's daughter.§这位**遗孀**掌管庄园三十年，最后把它留给了园丁的女儿。§
downplay§The company downplayed the leak for eleven days and then admitted it was four times larger than reported.§公司**淡化**了泄漏事故十一天，随后承认它比报道的大四倍。§down（向下）+ play（表现）→ 往小里说
dramatize§The film dramatizes a trial that in reality consisted of three hours of paperwork and one weary confession.§这部电影**戏剧化**了一场审判，而它实际上只是三小时的文书工作和一次疲惫的供认。§
drench§The storm drenched the site overnight, and two weeks of excavation records were lost to a single open trench.§暴雨一夜之间**浇透**了工地，两周的发掘记录因一条没盖的探沟而毁。§
drub§The visiting side was drubbed eleven to nil, and their manager resigned before the team bus left the ground.§客队被**痛击**十一比零，主教练在球队大巴离场前就辞了职。§
dual§The role is dual and the salary is not, which is the complaint every person who has held it has made.§这个职位是**双重的**，薪水却不是，这是每一任任职者都提过的抱怨。§du（二，同 duet 二重奏）
dubious§The provenance is dubious: the painting appears in no record before 1946 and in every catalogue after it.§这幅画的来源**可疑**——1946 年前不见于任何记录，此后却出现在每本图录里。§dub（二，同 double 双重）→ 心里两可
dumbfound§The verdict dumbfounded the courtroom, and even the defendant sat for a moment before he understood.§这个判决**惊呆**了整个法庭，连被告也愣了片刻才反应过来。§dumb（哑）+ found ← confound（使惊惶）
dupe§He was the dupe rather than the architect, and the sentencing judge said so in unusually plain language.§他是**被骗的傻瓜**而非策划者，量刑法官用异常直白的措辞这么说了。§
duplication§Duplication of effort cost the project a full year: two teams built the same module without ever meeting.§**重复劳动**让项目损失了整整一年——两个团队从未碰过面，却造了同一个模块。§du（二）+ plic（折叠，同 complicate 使复杂）
duplicity§The duplicity was systematic: one set of figures for the board, another for the regulator, and a third for the staff.§这种**表里不一**是成体系的——一套数字给董事会，一套给监管方，还有一套给员工。§du（二）+ plic（折叠）→ 两面派
durability§The durability of the material is its whole argument: it costs three times more and lasts forty years longer.§这种材料的**耐久性**就是它的全部理由——贵三倍，多用四十年。§dur（持久，同 endure 忍耐）
duration§For the duration of the repairs the museum kept one gallery open, and attendance fell by ninety percent.§在整个维修**期间**博物馆只保留一个展厅开放，参观人数下降了百分之九十。§
dwarf§The new tower dwarfs the cathedral that defined the skyline for six hundred years.§那座定义了六百年天际线的大教堂，在新塔面前**相形见绌**。§
dwindle§Membership dwindled from four thousand to ninety, and the last meeting was held in someone's kitchen.§会员从四千**锐减**到九十，最后一次会议是在某人的厨房里开的。§
earthy§Her earthy humour disarmed a courtroom that had spent two days on actuarial tables.§她那种**接地气的**幽默化解了一个已在精算表上耗了两天的法庭。§
ebb§Support for the plan ebbed slowly and then all at once, and the vote failed by a margin nobody had predicted.§对这项计划的支持先是慢慢**退潮**，然后一下子退光，投票以无人预料的差距落败。§
ebullient§He arrived ebullient and left silent, having discovered in between that the funding had already been spent.§他**兴高采烈**地到来，沉默地离开——期间发现经费已经花光了。§e-（出）+ bull（沸腾，同 boil 煮沸）→ 冒泡溢出来
eccentric§The eccentric old surveyor measured the same hill every spring for fifty years and left the best dataset anyone has.§这位**古怪的**老测量员五十年里每个春天测量同一座山，留下了现有最好的数据集。§ec-（离开）+ centr（中心）→ 偏离圆心
economic§The economic case was strong and the political case was hopeless, and only one of the two decided the outcome.§**经济上的**理由很充分，政治上的理由毫无希望，而决定结果的只有其中之一。§
economical§The economical option was rejected because it looked cheap, and the expensive one failed within two years.§**节省的**方案因为显得便宜而被否决，昂贵的那个两年内就失败了。§
economize§They economized on inspection and spent the savings, several times over, on the recall that followed.§他们在检验上**节省**，省下的钱在随后的召回中花掉了好几倍。§
edible§Only four of the eleven berries on this slope are edible, and two of the others closely resemble them.§这道山坡上十一种浆果只有四种**可食用**，另有两种与它们极为相似。§ed（吃）
edify§The lecture was meant to edify and mostly served to remind everyone how little the speaker had read.§这场讲座本意是**教化**，实际上主要提醒了所有人主讲者读得多么少。§aedi（房屋，同 edifice 大厦）+ fy（建造）→ 建造心灵
efface§Forty years of weather effaced the inscription, and the only record of it is a rubbing made in 1911.§四十年的风雨**磨去**了这段铭文，唯一的记录是 1911 年做的一份拓片。§ef-（出）+ face（面）→ 把表面抹掉
effective§The campaign was effective and dishonest, and the second fact has not stopped anyone from copying the first.§这场宣传**有效**且不诚实，后一点并未阻止任何人模仿前一点。§ef-（出）+ fect（做，同 perfect 完美的）
efficacious§The remedy is efficacious in the laboratory and useless in the field, because nobody takes it for eleven weeks.§这种疗法在实验室**有效**，在实际中无用，因为没人会连吃十一周。§
efficient§The most efficient route was also the one that passed four schools, so the council chose the slower one.§最**高效的**路线也是经过四所学校的那条，于是议会选了较慢的那条。§
effrontery§He had the effrontery to bill the client for the hours he spent correcting his own mistake.§他竟有这种**厚颜**，把纠正自己错误的工时也算给客户。§ef-（出）+ front（前额）→ 把脸伸出来不知羞
effusive§Her effusive thanks embarrassed the man who had simply returned a wallet he found on a bench.§她**热情洋溢的**感谢让那个只是归还了长椅上捡到钱包的人很不好意思。§ef-（出）+ fus（倒，同 confuse 混淆）→ 感情倒出来
egalitarian§The scheme is egalitarian in design and regressive in effect, because the poorest households cannot claim it.§这个方案设计上是**平等主义的**，效果上却是累退的，因为最穷的家庭申请不了。§
egoism§His egoism is not vanity but a genuine inability to imagine that other people's reasons are as real as his.§他的**自我中心**不是虚荣，而是真的无法想象别人的理由和他的一样真实。§ego（我）
egotistical§The most egotistical passage in the memoir describes a meeting the other four participants remember differently.§回忆录里最**自我中心的**一段描述了一场会议，另外四位与会者的记忆截然不同。§
egregious§The error was egregious enough that the journal retracted the paper without waiting for the authors to reply.§这个错误**离谱**到期刊没等作者回复就撤了稿。§e-（出）+ greg（群，同 gregarious 群居的）→ 出格到人群外
elaborate§The excuse was elaborate where a simple one would have worked, which is what made everybody suspicious.§本来简单的借口就够用，这个却**精心繁复**，这才让所有人起了疑。§e-（出）+ labor（劳动）→ 下足功夫做出来
elate§The result elated a team that had expected, quite reasonably, to finish last in a league of sixteen.§一支相当合理地预期会在十六队联赛中垫底的队伍，被这个结果弄得**欣喜若狂**。§e-（出）+ lat（举，同 relate 关联）→ 情绪被抬起来
elation§The elation lasted a week, and the invoice for the celebration arrived just as it was wearing off.§这份**兴高采烈**持续了一周，庆祝活动的账单恰在它消退时寄到。§
elegance§The elegance of the proof is that it needs no case analysis at all, which took ninety years to find.§这个证明的**优雅**在于完全不需要分情况讨论，而这一点花了九十年才找到。§eleg（挑选，同 elect 选举）→ 挑得精当
elementary§The mistake was elementary, and the fact that four reviewers missed it says more than the mistake does.§这个错误很**初级**，而四位评审都没看出来这件事比错误本身更说明问题。§element（元素）
elevate§The appointment elevated a competent administrator into a job that required a very different kind of person.§这次任命把一位称职的行政人员**提拔**到一个需要截然不同类型的人的岗位上。§e-（出）+ lev（轻，同 levity 轻浮）→ 举起来
eliminate§They eliminated three of the four explanations in a single afternoon and spent nine years on the fourth.§他们一个下午就**排除**了四种解释中的三种，第四种花了九年。§e-（出）+ limin（门槛，同 limit 界限）→ 赶出门去
elitist§The scholarship was called elitist by people who had not noticed that most recipients were the first in their families to finish school.§这项奖学金被人称作**精英主义的**，而那些人没注意到多数受奖者是家里第一个念完学的。§
elliptical§His answer was elliptical enough that both sides left the room believing he had agreed with them.§他的回答**含糊省略**到双方离场时都以为他同意了自己。§
elocutionist§The elocutionist trained four generations of broadcasters, and you can still hear her vowels on the radio.§这位**演说训练师**培养了四代播音员，如今广播里仍能听见她的元音。§e-（出）+ loqu（说，同 eloquent 雄辩的）
eloquent§The most eloquent moment was the silence: he stopped for four seconds and the room understood everything.§最**动人心弦**的时刻是那阵沉默——他停了四秒，全场就都明白了。§e-（出）+ loqu（说，同 colloquial 口语的）
elude§The pattern eluded four teams for a decade and fell to a student who plotted the data upside down.§这个规律**躲过**四支团队十年，最后被一个把数据倒过来画的学生逮到。§e-（出）+ lud（玩，同 illusion 幻觉）→ 玩着溜走
elusive§The species is so elusive that the first photograph of a living animal was taken in 2007.§这个物种**难以捉摸**到第一张活体照片是 2007 年才拍到的。§
embarrassment§The embarrassment was public and the correction was not, which is how the false figure survived four more years.§**难堪**是公开的，更正则不是，所以那个错误数字又活了四年。§
embellish§He embellished the story a little each time, and by the fortieth telling the fish weighed nine kilograms.§他每讲一次就**添油加醋**一点，讲到第四十遍时那条鱼已重九公斤。§em-（使）+ bell（美丽，同 beauty 美）
embellishment§Strip the embellishment and a remarkable thing remains: a nineteen-year-old walked four hundred miles alone.§剥掉那些**润饰**，剩下的事仍然了不起——一个十九岁的人独自走了四百英里。§
embitter§Two decades of small refusals embittered a man who had begun as the most generous person in the department.§二十年的小小拒绝让一个起初是全系最慷慨的人**心生怨恨**。§em-（使）+ bitter（苦）
emblem§The bird became an emblem of the movement almost by accident: it was simply the easiest thing to draw.§这只鸟几乎是偶然地成了这场运动的**象征**——它只是最好画的东西。§em-（在内）+ bl ← ball（投掷，同 ballistic 弹道的）→ 嵌进去的图案
embodiment§The building is the embodiment of an argument its architect made in a lecture nobody remembers.§这栋建筑是其建筑师在一场无人记得的讲座中提出的论点的**具体化身**。§em-（使）+ body（身体）
embolden§The first successful appeal emboldened eleven other families to file, and nine of them eventually won.§第一次上诉成功**鼓舞**了另外十一个家庭去提起诉讼，其中九家最终胜诉。§em-（使）+ bold（大胆）
embrace§The industry embraced the standard within two years, having fought it for the previous nine.§这个行业两年内就**接纳**了这项标准，而此前九年一直在抵制它。§em-（在内）+ brace（手臂，同 bracelet 手镯）
embroil§A single email embroiled the department in a dispute that took two lawyers and eleven months to end.§一封邮件把整个部门**卷入**一场纠纷，动用两名律师、耗时十一个月才了结。§em-（使）+ broil（争吵）
eminent§The most eminent scholar in the field was also the one who most readily admitted what he did not know.§这个领域最**杰出的**学者也是最痛快承认自己不懂什么的那位。§e-（出）+ min（突出，同 prominent 显著的）
emotional§The argument was emotional on both sides and factual on neither, and the vote followed the volume.§双方的争论都是**情绪化的**，都不基于事实，投票结果跟着音量走。§
